items.title: Flip Phillips interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 11, 1996
items.q: The rhythm section you had the best. Hank Jones, Oscar Peterson, Buddy Rich, Louis Bellson, Jo Jones, Gene Krupa.

ctx.x: Who else was on the tour? I know there was a lot of different people.

At the beginning, oh, at the very beginning we had everybody. He put together the best in jazz, the best in music, the best players. He was the only man that I know that could do a thing like that, to assemble a group like that. Well you had, your tenor saxophones was Coleman Hawkins, Lester Young, Ben Webster, Illinois Jacquet, Stan Getz, Sonny Stitt — I hope I don’t leave anybody out — all the best. On the trumpets he had Roy Eldridge, Charlie Shavers, Dizzy Gillespie, Sweets, Fats Navarro, all the best in…

items.title: Jones Hank — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] The band was Eldridge, Tommy Turk, Parker, Flip Phillips, Prez. [INTERVIEWEE] Yeah, Tommy was on that. ... [INTERVIEWER] No, it was Eldridge, Tommy Turk, Parker, Phillips, Hank Jones, Ray Brown and Buddy Rich. [INTERVIEWEE] Yeah, that was a JPT thing.

ctx.x: In 1947, how did you get to Jazz at the Philharmonic? How did I come to be?

You see, I was working on 52nd St. I think with Lips, or at The Spotlight. Norman Grantz had heard about my playing has supposed and he… His piano player was leaving. I forget who it was at the time, but they were leaving the group and he needed somebody to go on tour with him. He was leaving to go on tour in several days. So, that was my first engagement. I went out with him on that tour. Subsequently, I did maybe a Taurus because he used to go on tour twice a year. That was once in the spring and once in the…
You made some recordings with Parker.
